quizName: Hardest Questions in New mexico Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:
questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Which one is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Be as effective as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Which one is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: When riding, wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, you can help others see you by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that are not tucked in.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Provide a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction for motorcycle tires. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal checking routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal checking routine.
questions.explanation: For your safety, you need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good color to wear to be seen?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding a motorcycle. This helps other drivers see you. Wear bright clothing any time you ride, day or night.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts the wearer's vision to the sides.
Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
Makes it more difficult for the wearer to control their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet while riding greatly reduces your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Inspect your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually results in no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can change how the motorcycle handles.
Is encouraged to help riders practice different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: The only way to rid your body of alcohol is through:
questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Not use turn signals unless you are traveling at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles, look 12 seconds ahead, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other drivers to your intentions.
Should not be used if no vehicles are near the motorcycle.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other drivers to your intentions.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are very vulnerable. Always use your turn signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use them any time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and use all the controls easily.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to give you a better grip on the handlebars.
Not be worn because they make it harder to use the controls.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or other durable material when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can improve visibility by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What can help reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.
